title: Maximum Number of K-Divisible Components
summary: Given an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a 2D array of edges, along with a values array and an integer k, determine the maximum number of components in the tree where each component's value (sum of node values) is divisible by k by removing any set of edges.
statement: Given an undirected tree with nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, and a 2D array of edges, along with a values array and an integer k, determine the maximum number of components in the tree where each component's value (sum of node values) is divisible by k by removing any set of edges.
constraints: edges forms a tree and the total value sum is divisible by k.
Remove edges so every resulting component sum is divisible by k; maximize component count.
hints: A subtree whose total is divisible by k can be detached without harming the remainder.
Compute subtree sums bottom-up and count every divisible sum.
DFS children, add their returned totals, count total modulo k equal to zero.
Because the whole sum is divisible, greedily cutting every divisible subtree yields valid remaining components and cannot reduce the optimum.
editorial: Because the whole sum is divisible, greedily cutting every divisible subtree yields valid remaining components and cannot reduce the optimum.

tests.explanation: Cutting one suitable edge produces two components whose sums are both divisible by six.
Postorder subtree sums identify the maximum divisible component cuts.
